name: Code test evidence and maintainability evaluation
description: Aggregate independently executed test results, check a structured-output envelope, and summarize separately supplied requirement and maintainability reviews without executing submitted code.

test_results.passed.description: Nonnegative passed-test count imported from an independent isolated test runner. Must not exceed test_results.total. Keep runner version and task identity in provenance metadata.

test_results.total.description: Nonnegative executed-test count from the same run. Zero executed tests is not applicable, not a successful run.

prediction.structured_output.description: Model-produced JSON object envelope, such as an object containing a code string. This metric parses the envelope only.

checks.requirements_valid.description: Imported independent requirement-check result for a documented task specification. This engine does not test program behavior or execute the code.

human_review.maintainability_score.description: Independent code-maintenance review, integer 0-4: 0 is opaque or structurally unusable; 1 has major readability or design problems; 2 is understandable with substantial maintenance risks; 3 is clear with minor issues; 4 is clear, cohesive, and documented to the project's stated conventions. Review actual code and context separately; synthetic examples contain illustrative annotations only.

metadata.dataset_version.description: Optional immutable dataset/split version for traceability. Not required or verified by this scorer.

metadata.model_version.description: Optional model/checkpoint version that produced the predictions. Not required or verified by this scorer.

human_review.reviewer_id.description: Optional independent reviewer identifier. The scorer does not authenticate the reviewer or validate qualifications; synthetic examples do not identify a real reviewer.

human_review.rubric_version.description: Optional version of the human-review instructions used to assign ratings. The scorer does not verify adherence to that rubric.

test_results.runner_version.description: Optional independent test-runner and suite version. Traceability only; no run is performed or verified here.

metrics.name: Independent test pass fraction
metrics.description: Mean per-item passed/total ratio from imported independently executed test counts.
metrics.limitations: No tests are executed by this engine. This is a macro average of per-item test fractions, not HumanEval pass@k, a pooled test pass rate, or proof of test completeness.

metrics.name: JSON envelope syntax
metrics.description: Fraction of submitted structured-output strings that parse as strict JSON objects.
metrics.limitations: Parses the JSON envelope only. Code syntax, code safety, API behavior, and application-schema validity are not evaluated.

metrics.name: Imported requirement-check pass rate
metrics.description: Fraction of independently supplied requirement-check flags that are true.
metrics.limitations: Trust depends on an external checker and a documented task specification. A supplied true flag is not independently verified here.

metrics.name: Human-reviewed maintainability
metrics.description: Mean independently reviewed maintainability score normalized from 0-4 to 0-1.
metrics.limitations: This imports an independent review score; the engine neither performs the review nor verifies reviewer identity. Missing reviews are excluded and reduce coverage.

limitations: This is a reusable evaluation template, not an official benchmark scorer. All targets are unset; calibrate thresholds and minimum coverage on a representative held-out dataset. Scores are not automatically used as screening gates or RL rewards.
Submitted code and test commands are never executed by this metrics pack. Run them in your own isolated evaluator before importing results.
A high score cannot establish code security, absence of defects, or sufficient test coverage.
Fixture test counts and reviews are fabricated examples and must not be reported as executed test evidence.
Unused metadata and review-provenance fields are optional traceability suggestions; their presence, authenticity, and types are not validated unless a metric references them.
